input.reasoning:
Estimate built bottom-up from story points using a velocity assumption of ~1 point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended engineering effort, then split across roles by task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, QA, DevOps). Total points = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21 = 81. Applied role mix per task type:
- PW-1 (CI/staging, 5 pts): DevOps-led, some Backend support.
- PW-2 (Design system, 8 pts): Frontend-led.
- PW-3 (Auth, 8 pts): Backend-led, Frontend for UI, QA for testing.
- PW-4 (RBAC, 13 pts): Backend-led, Frontend for UI enforcement, QA.
- PW-5 (Dashboard, 8 pts): Frontend-led, Backend for APIs, QA.
- PW-6 (Invoices, 5 pts): Frontend + Backend + QA.
- PW-7 (Payments, 13 pts): Backend-heavy (Stripe/webhooks), QA critical, some DevOps for infra/monitoring.
- PW-8 (Migration, 21 pts): Backend-heavy (ETL scripts), DevOps for environment/cutover, QA for data validation.

Converted point-hours to role hours per task, then summed per role. Checked against FTE capacity over an assumed ~12-week (480 hour/FTE) delivery window:
- Backend Developer: 1.5 FTE => ~720 hours capacity over 12 weeks. Allocated 690 hours — within capacity, high utilization.
- Frontend Developer: 1.0 FTE => ~480 hours capacity. Allocated 360 hours — comfortable.
- QA Engineer: 0.6 FTE => ~288 hours capacity. Allocated 190 hours — within capacity.
- DevOps Engineer: 0.4 FTE => ~192 hours capacity. Allocated 130 hours — within capacity, but this role is thin and is a scheduling constraint for PW-1 and PW-8 cutover windows.

Non-labour costs added for Stripe integration sandbox/compliance review, staging/cloud infra during migration, and a data migration validation/reconciliation contingency line (given the scale — 400k customers / 2M invoice lines — and the note that no historical actuals exist to calibrate migration effort, this is a key risk area).

Priority breakdown aggregates task cost by priority label. Scenario range reflects uncertainty inherent in a no-actuals estimate, particularly around PW-8 (migration) and PW-7 (payment reconciliation edge cases), which are the two highest-risk/urgent-or-high items.

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration setup, PCI/compliance review, and sandbox testing fees
Staging/cloud infrastructure costs during CI setup and migration (compute, storage)
Legacy data migration contingency (reconciliation tooling, extra validation passes)
Project management / contingency buffer (10% of labour)

scenarios.name: Pessimistic (migration complexity, payment reconciliation rework, DevOps bottleneck)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend/velocity data) exist for this project; hour allocations are derived from story points using an assumed ~6-7 hours-per-point blended rate, not from past performance.
Delivery window assumed at ~12 weeks (480 hours/FTE), used only to sanity-check role hours against available FTE capacity, not as a firm commitment date.

DevOps Engineer is staffed at only 0.4 FTE (~192hrs over the window) and is a capacity constraint for PW-1 (pipeline setup) and PW-8 (migration cutover); delays in DevOps availability could push the timeline even though cost stays similar.
PW-8 (Legacy data migration) effort is highly uncertain given no actuals and the scale (400k records / 2M invoice lines); a dedicated reconciliation/contingency line has been added.
PW-7 (Payment integration) assumes standard Stripe card flows; deeper reconciliation edge cases or multi-currency support would increase scope beyond this estimate.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE is assumed to test across all backend/frontend workstreams; testing is allocated proportionally to task risk (heaviest on PW-3, PW-4, PW-7, PW-8).
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for infra and compliance fees since no vendor quotes were supplied.
A 10% labour contingency/PM buffer is included given the lack of historical actuals to calibrate against.

reductions.description: Defer PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a later phase and use a third-party UI kit (e.g. Angular Material) instead of building custom shared components now.
reductions.effect: Removes ~130 hours of Frontend Developer time from this phase; component library can be built incrementally as real screens require it.

reductions.description: Reduce QA scope on Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) to smoke testing only, deferring full regression coverage until post-launch.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~50 QA hours; slightly raises risk of undetected edge-case bugs in lower-priority features.

reductions.description: Descope real-time reconciliation dashboard from PW-7 and ship basic webhook handling only; add reconciliation UI in a later release.
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend Developer and QA hours on PW-7 by roughly 60 hours combined.

reductions.description: Phase the legacy data migration (PW-8): migrate customer records first, defer invoice-line migration to a follow-up sprint after the portal launches.
reductions.effect: Cuts current-phase Backend and DevOps hours on PW-8 by ~90 hours and removes part of the migration contingency non-labour line; remaining invoice-line migration is billed in a later project phase.

reductions.description: Drop the 10% PM/contingency buffer to 5% by tightening scope definition on Urgent items before kickoff.
reductions.effect: Halves the contingency line; increases risk of budget overrun if estimates prove too tight, especially on PW-8.
